title: ZFS DMU block store backend
description:
Implement ZfsDmuStore using the userspace DMU object API (stoa-b37a7fd4) as a block store backend for both transit and reader.

Depends on: pluggable backend epic (stoa-5c9f1a38) and ZFS DMU userspace API (stoa-b37a7fd4).

## Why this is compelling

ZFS DMU already implements what the block store layer needs: content-addressed immutable blocks, SHA-256/SHA-512 checksums per block, native deduplication (articles that appear on multiple groups or are re-injected are stored once), copy-on-write, and instant snapshots for backup. The CID-to-object-ID mapping is a single SQLite table.

## What needs doing

- Implement `ZfsDmuStore: IpfsStore` (transit) and `ZfsDmuBlockStore: IpfsBlockStore` (reader) using the `usenet-ipfs-zfs-dmu` crate
  - `put`: write bytes via `object_write`; record `(cid, object_id)` in a SQLite index table; skip if CID already in index
  - `get`: look up `object_id` from index by CID; call `object_read(object_id)`; map miss → `None` / `NotFound`
- Add `[backend.zfs_dmu]` config section: `dataset` (ZFS dataset name or zvol path), `index_db` (path to the CID→object_id SQLite file)
- IPNS: disable (same as filesystem backend — no IPFS network node)
- Verify dataset is accessible and writable at startup; emit a clear error if ZFS kernel module is not loaded or dataset does not exist
- GC: unpin by removing the index entry and calling `object_free(object_id)`; ZFS dedup table handles the rest
- Runbook section: ZFS dataset creation (`zfs create`), dedup property (`zfs set dedup=sha256`), snapshot strategy

## Acceptance criteria
- Round-trip test using the ZFS DMU API crate (can use a loopback pool in CI if kernel module available, otherwise mark as integration-test requiring ZFS)
- CID computed locally matches what Kubo would produce for the same bytes
- Deduplication: writing the same article bytes twice results in one DMU object (verified via `zfs list -o dedupratio`)
